list.name: board
list.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM boards WHERE id LIKE 'linear:%' ORDER BY name
list.label: Issue board

list.name: contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1
list.label: Contributor

options.content:
## GenAI Adoption — Executive Summary
*How much of this team's delivery is AI-assisted, and what it costs or saves.* Every number below is measured from git history and the agent's own session records — none of it is self-reported or estimated.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id WHERE c.status='assisted' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(c.status<>'undetermined')/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0),0) v FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')/NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

SELECT COUNT(*) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed') AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.session) v FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id WHERE e.session<>'' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

options.content:
### Does AI-assisted work ship faster?
Cycle time for issues whose commits carry an AI-attribution trailer, against those that don't. **A measured comparison, not an estimate** — if the *Not AI-assisted* count is zero there is no control group yet and the delta means nothing. That count is shown deliberately.

panels.title: Median cycle — AI-assisted

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ltm)/60,1) v FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t WHERE ai=1

panels.description: Issues whose commits carry an attribution trailer, against those that do not. Read it as a description, not a verdict: harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer AI-assisted cycle usually reflects which issues were chosen, not the agent slowing them down.

panels.title: Delta

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
   (SELECT AVG(ltm) FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) a WHERE ai=0)
 - (SELECT AVG(ltm) FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) b WHERE ai=1), 0) / 60 v

panels.description: Issues whose commits carry an attribution trailer, against those that do not. Read it as a description, not a verdict: harder work tends to get handed to an agent, so a longer AI-assisted cycle usually reflects which issues were chosen, not the agent slowing them down.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT issue_key AS `Issue`,
       CASE ai WHEN 1 THEN 'AI-assisted' ELSE 'not AI-assisted' END AS `Attribution`,
       ROUND(ltm/60, 1) AS `Cycle hours`,
       resolution_date AS `Resolved`
FROM (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t
ORDER BY resolution_date DESC

options.content:
### Trend
Use the **Granularity** control above to switch between daily, weekly and monthly buckets.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       SUM(c.status='assisted') AS `assisted`,
       SUM(c.status='undetermined') AS `undetermined`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.title: Agent edits & lines written over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       COUNT(*) AS `agent edits`,
       SUM(e.lines_added) AS `lines added`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')
             /NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `accept %`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

SELECT DATE(i.resolution_date) AS `time`,
       SUM(t.ai = 1) AS `AI-assisted`,
       SUM(t.ai = 0) AS `not AI-assisted`
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN (
SELECT i.issue_key,
       i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
       i.resolution_date,
       COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
FROM issues i
JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
LEFT JOIN commits c
       ON c.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes, i.resolution_date
) t ON t.issue_key = i.issue_key
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

options.content:
### Where the AI is being applied
Purpose is classified from the commit itself, not self-reported.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.purpose AS `metric`, COUNT(*) AS `value`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=c.repo_id
WHERE c.status='assisted' AND c.purpose<>'' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY c.purpose ORDER BY `value` DESC

SELECT e.tool AS `Tool`,
       SUM(e.outcome='accepted') AS `Accepted`,
       SUM(e.outcome='rejected') AS `Rejected`,
       SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')) AS `Decided`,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(e.outcome='accepted')
             /NULLIF(SUM(e.outcome IN ('accepted','rejected','failed')),0),1) AS `Accept %`
FROM whodunit_events e JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=e.repo_id
WHERE e.tool<>'' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY e.tool ORDER BY `Decided` DESC

SELECT LEFT(s.session,8) AS `Session`,
       ROUND((s.last_seen-s.first_seen)/60000000000) AS `Minutes`,
       s.user_messages AS `Prompts`,
       s.tool_calls AS `Tool calls`,
       s.distinct_tools AS `Tools`
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=s.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
ORDER BY s.first_seen DESC

panels.title: Commits — assisted vs the rest

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS `time`,
       SUM(c.status = 'assisted') AS `assisted`,
       SUM(c.status <> 'assisted') AS `not assisted`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
  AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Stacked, so the bar height is total commit volume and the blue share is adoption. A flat blue band before instrumentation is expected — those commits predate whodunit and are not evidence that no agent was used.

panels.title: Issues opened vs completed

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DATE(i.created_date) AS `time`,
       COUNT(*) AS `opened`,
       SUM(i.status = 'DONE') AS `completed`
FROM issues i JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
  AND i.created_date IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
GROUP BY `time` ORDER BY `time`

panels.description: Both series are keyed on the date an issue was opened, so 'completed' is how many of that week's issues are now done — not how many were closed that week. Recent weeks therefore look worse than they will.
